## Description

A green paramecium (80–150 µm, ~110 × 50 µm) with hundreds of endosymbiotic *Chlorella* (~300–700 per
cell) in perialgal vacuoles. The algae divide inside with light and pass maltose to the host: in light
green cells grow even without food; in the dark they lose algae and depend on bacteria again. At
division the algae are shared between the daughters; those left without algae recover them by eating
free *Chlorella*. It gathers where there is light.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 6 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Endosymbionts](../../mechanics/symbioses.md) that grow with light, are lost in the dark, are shared binomially at
division and are taken up from eaten *Chlorella*. With algae it follows light through an avoiding
reaction when it gets darker (a `step_down` response). Maximum load, rates and photosynthate fraction
estimated.

- Müller H., Geller W. (1993) Maximum growth rates of aquatic ciliated protozoa: the dependence on body size and temperature reconsidered. Arch. Hydrobiol. 126: 315–327 (allometric µmax estimate, not a measurement of the species).

## Not implemented yet

- No coexistence experiment with *P. caudatum* by use of space (Gause).
- The algal load is a number, not individual algae in vacuoles.
- Helix radius and period are estimates (of the order of Bullington 1925 and Jennings 1906).
- Trichocysts are a defence gene, not discharged organelles that can be counted.
- Contractile vacuole period in fresh water estimated; cytosol osmolarity taken from *P. caudatum*.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares photosymbionts with *Mesodinium*; uses *Chlorella* as its source.
